1.title: Cloud Concepts, Google Cloud Infrastructure and Service Models
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Cloud Concepts, Google Cloud Infrastructure and Service Models. It covers the exam area one. Digital transformation with Google Cloud. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. one point two Describe fundamental cloud concepts: the business use case and benefits of private cloud, hybrid cloud and multicloud. Fundamental networking concepts. The components of Google Cloud's network (regions, zones, edge locations). The benefits and tradeoffs of I A A S, pass and sass. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Digital transformation with Google Cloud (about eighteen percent). Exam format: ninety minutes and fifty to sixty multiple-choice questions. Validated against: the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide.

1.title: Cloud architectures
1.text: Cloud architectures. The figure shows this: Private cloud, hybrid cloud and multicloud compared.

1.title: Cloud architectures, continued
1.text: Cloud architectures. On-premises. What it is: Your own data center. Business use case: Full control; high upfront cost, slow to scale. Public cloud. What it is: Resources shared on a provider's infrastructure, paid by use. Business use case: Speed, scale and low startup cost. Private cloud. What it is: Cloud-style resources for one organization. Business use case: Strict control or regulation. Hybrid cloud. What it is: On-premises or private plus public cloud, connected. Business use case: Move step by step; keep sensitive or legacy systems on site.

1.title: Cloud architectures, continued
1.text: Cloud architectures. Multicloud. What it is: More than one public cloud provider. Business use case: Avoid lock-in, choose the best service for each job, resilience. Exam tip: Hybrid equals on-premises plus cloud. Multicloud equals more than one cloud provider. Hybrid is the answer for "keep some systems in our own data center".

1.title: Networking basics
1.text: Networking basics. I P address. The numeric address of a device on a network. Domain name service (D N S). Turns names such as example.com into I P addresses. Latency. The delay before data arrives; lower is better. Bandwidth. The amount of data a connection can carry; higher is better. Latency depends on distance, so placing resources near users helps.

1.title: Google Cloud's global infrastructure
1.text: Google Cloud's global infrastructure. Region. A geographic area with several zones. Zone. A deployment area inside a region, with independent power, cooling and networking; a failure in one zone should not affect others. Edge location. A network point of presence close to users that caches content and connects to Google's network. Global network. Google's own fiber network, including subsea cables, that connects regions and edge locations. Multiple zones give high availability; multiple regions give disaster recovery and lower latency for global users. The network carries traffic on Google's own private backbone instead of the public internet where possible, for speed and security. Exam tip: Zone equals failure domain inside a region. Region equals geographic area. Spread across zones for availability, across regions for disaster recovery and reach.

1.title: Service models: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS
1.text: Service models: I A A S, pass and sass. Infrastructure as a Service. You get: Virtual machines, storage, networks. You manage: Operating system, applications, data. Example on Google Cloud: Compute Engine. Platform as a Service. You get: A platform to build and run apps. You manage: Applications and data. Example on Google Cloud: Cloud Run, App Engine, Big Query. Software as a Service. You get: A finished application. You manage: Your data, users and settings. Example on Google Cloud: Google Workspace, Looker. Control and flexibility. I A A S: Highest. pass: Medium. sass: Lowest. Effort and staffing. I A A S: Highest. pass: Medium. sass: Lowest. Speed to value. I A A S: Slower. pass: Fast. sass: Fastest. Customization. I A A S: Most. pass: Some. sass: Least. Choose by need: maximum control to I A A S; build apps without managing servers to pass; a ready tool for users to sass. Exam tip: The more the provider manages, the less you control and the less you must staff. I A A S equals most control, sass equals least.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A hospital must keep patient records in its own data center but wants to use cloud analytics for other workloads. Which architecture fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Hybrid cloud, connecting on-premises and public cloud. Hybrid cloud connects on-premises systems with public cloud services.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A company wants to avoid depending on one provider and chooses the best service from several public clouds. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A multicloud strategy, using several providers. Using more than one public cloud provider is multicloud.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A single data center failure in a region must not stop an application. What is the best design? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Spread the application across several zones. Zones are independent failure domains; spreading across zones gives high availability.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which term describes the delay before data arrives from a server? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Latency, the delay in delivery. Latency is the delay; lower latency means faster responses.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A startup wants to deploy its own web application without managing servers or operating systems. Which service model fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: pass, because it provides a platform to run apps. Platform as a Service lets a team run its own code without managing the underlying servers.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company needs full control of the operating system and installed software on its servers in the cloud. Which model fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: I A A S, with virtual machines it manages. I A A S gives the most control, and the customer manages the operating system and above.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is hybrid cloud? Answer: On-premises or private resources connected with public cloud. Question two. What is multicloud? Answer: Using more than one public cloud provider. Question three. What is a zone? Answer: A deployment area inside a region with independent infrastructure.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does D N S do? Answer: Turns names into I P addresses. Question five. Which model gives the most control? Answer: I A A S. Question six. Is Compute Engine I A A S or pass? Answer: I A A S.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Architectures: on-premises, public, private, hybrid (on-premises plus cloud), multicloud (several clouds). Network: I P, D N S, latency (delay), bandwidth (capacity). Google Cloud network: regions, zones (failure domains), edge locations, global fiber network. Service models: I A A S most control, pass apps and data, sass least effort.
